name: video_editing
description: People asking for help with video editing, YouTube channels, short-form social video, thumbnails and UGC.
_comment_phrases: Exact phrases a BUYER writes. Each is searched as an exact match, so word
order matters: 'need a video editor' and 'video editor needed' are two
different searches and both are worth having.
They get packed into as few queries as X's ~512-character limit allows
(about 11 per query), so adding a phrase is cheap until it tips a batch
over — check the query count with --dry-run after editing.
Put the highest-yield phrases first: --max-queries truncates from the end.
Do NOT add bare keywords like 'video editing' or 'youtube'. That is what
the old scraper searched, and it returned mostly people chatting about
video rather than anyone wanting to pay for it.
phrases: looking for a short form editor
looking for a social media manager
_comment_language: X's lang: operator. Set to null to search every language, but note the classifier's patterns are English-only, so anything else scores as noise.
_comment_extra_operators: Appended verbatim to every query. -filter:replies and -filter:retweets are
always applied and do not belong here.
Server-side negatives are tempting ('-"dm me"') but were left out on
purpose: real job posts say 'DM me your portfolio' constantly, so a
negative there removes good leads. Filtering sellers is the classifier's
job, where it can weigh the whole post instead of one phrase.
min_faves:1 is a reasonable addition if the volume is still too high.
